items.text: Python 3.8 still receives security updates from the Python core team.
items.truth: Python 3.8 reached end of life on 2024-10-07.

items.text: Python 3.9 still receives security fixes.
items.truth: Python 3.9 reached end of life in October 2025.

items.text: Node.js 16 is an active LTS release.
items.truth: Node.js 16 reached end of life on 2023-09-11.

items.text: Node.js 18 is still in maintenance LTS.
items.truth: Node.js 18 reached end of life on 2025-04-30.

items.text: Node.js 20 is still supported by the Node.js project.
items.truth: Node.js 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30.

items.text: Heroku offers free dynos for hobby projects.
items.truth: Heroku removed free dynos on 2022-11-28.

items.text: GitHub Actions still provides the ubuntu-20.04 hosted runner image.
items.truth: The ubuntu-20.04 runner image was retired in April 2025.

items.text: CentOS Linux 8 is a supported distribution.
items.truth: CentOS Linux 8 reached end of life on 2021-12-31.

items.text: Create React App is the recommended way to start a new React project.
items.truth: Create React App was deprecated on 2025-02-14; React docs recommend frameworks or Vite.

items.text: Django 3.2 is still under extended support.
items.truth: Django 3.2 extended support ended in April 2024.

items.text: Django 4.2 LTS is still under extended support.
items.truth: Django 4.2 LTS extended support ended in April 2026.

items.text: The request npm package is actively maintained.
items.truth: request was deprecated in February 2020.

items.text: Rust's newest edition is the 2021 edition.
items.truth: The Rust 2024 edition was stabilised in Rust 1.85 (February 2025).

items.text: Ruby 3.0 is still supported with security fixes.
items.truth: Ruby 3.0 reached end of life on 2024-04-23.

items.text: PHP 8.0 still receives security updates.
items.truth: PHP 8.0 reached end of life on 2023-11-26.

items.text: Bootstrap 4 still receives bug fixes.
items.truth: Bootstrap 4 reached end of life on 2023-01-01.

items.text: AngularJS 1.x receives long-term support from Google.
items.truth: AngularJS long-term support ended on 2021-12-31.

items.text: Google Domains is accepting new domain registrations.
items.truth: Google Domains was sold to Squarespace in 2023 and migrations completed in 2024.

items.text: Debian 12 (bookworm) is the current stable release.
items.truth: Debian 13 (trixie) became stable on 2025-08-09; bookworm is oldstable.

items.text: Docker Desktop is free for every company regardless of size.
items.truth: Since 2021-08-31 larger companies need a paid subscription.

items.text: The latest Ubuntu LTS release is 22.04.
items.truth: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (April 2024) and 26.04 LTS (April 2026) have since shipped; 22.04 remains supported.

items.text: The latest Python release series is 3.12.
items.truth: Python 3.13 (Oct 2024) and 3.14 (Oct 2025) have since been released.

items.text: React's latest major version is 18.
items.truth: React 19 was released in December 2024.

items.text: Django's latest long-term support release is 4.2.
items.truth: Django 5.2 LTS was released in April 2025.

items.text: Redis is licensed under the three-clause BSD license.
items.truth: Redis moved to RSALv2/SSPL in March 2024 and added AGPLv3 with Redis 8 in May 2025.

items.text: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS is within its standard five-year support window.
items.truth: Standard support ended 2025-05-31; only Expanded Security Maintenance continues.

items.text: Moment.js is actively developed and recommended for new projects.
items.truth: Moment.js has been in maintenance mode since September 2020 and its own docs discourage new use.

items.text: Python 3.12 receives security fixes until October 2028.
items.truth: Correct per the Python release schedule.

items.text: Python 3.11 is supported until October 2027.
items.truth: Correct per the Python release schedule.

items.text: Node.js 22 is a Long Term Support release.
items.truth: Node.js 22 entered LTS in October 2024 and is supported until April 2027.

items.text: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is supported until 2029.
items.truth: Standard support runs to April 2029.

items.text: GitHub Actions is free to use on public repositories.
items.truth: Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories.

items.text: Python 2 reached end of life in January 2020.
items.truth: Python 2.7 end of life was 2020-01-01.

items.text: Express 5 requires Node.js 18 or later.
items.truth: Express 5.0 dropped support for Node.js below 18.

items.text: Debian 13 (trixie) is the current stable release.
items.truth: Released 2025-08-09.

items.text: Django 5.2 is a long-term support release.
items.truth: Django 5.2 LTS, April 2025, supported until April 2028.

items.text: The Linux kernel is licensed under GPLv2.
items.truth: Unchanged.

items.text: Homebrew is available for both macOS and Linux.
items.truth: Unchanged.

items.text: Rust publishes a new stable release every six weeks.
items.truth: Unchanged release cadence.
